title: Binary search: search on answer
summary: Slowest speed that finishes every load within hours (one load per hour, partial hours count). feasible(speed) flips once from no to yes, so binary search the speed. O(n log m).
code: # Feasibility only improves as speed grows, so search for the first feasible speed.
return sum((load + speed - 1) // speed for load in loads) <= hours
triggers: 'smallest capacity, speed or days such that...' or 'minimize the maximum'
a yes/no feasibility test that flips once as the answer grows
prompts: A print shop must finish all orders within a fixed number of hours. Each hour the press works on a single order at one pages-per-hour rate, and a partial hour counts as a full one. What is the slowest rate that meets the deadline?
Parcels leave in their original order over a fixed number of days, each day's truck carrying as many as fit. What is the smallest truck capacity that finishes on time?
invariant: Every speed below left is infeasible and right is feasible; when they meet, left is the smallest feasible speed.
mantra: If feasibility is monotonic, binary search the answer, not the array.
pitfalls: Search the answer range [1, max(loads)], not the input indices.
Ceiling division: (load + speed - 1) // speed; floor loses the partial hour.
feasible(mid) keeps mid (right = mid); otherwise left = mid + 1.

anchors.name: Split Array Largest Sum
